Now it's dusk. Red light of the sunset is streaming through the narrow windows of the north tower, where you have come to catch your breath in what seems to be the ruined and decaying remains of a study or council chamber of some kind. Outside, you can hear the howls of beasts—hyenas, lions, jackals, wild dogs—in the distance, fading and then growing stronger as something stirs them up, and then fading again, from the outer courtyard beyond the towers. The stench of rotting sulphurous flesh and a faint tinge of ash in your mouth rises from the inner courtyard on the other side. A flicker of firelight gleams from the windows and the open door of the main keep.
